subject.title: [Bug] Telegram exec approval bubble not dismissed after clicking approve

question: Should maintainers close/replace the open conflicting cross-repo candidate before queuing a narrow current-runtime fix for this issue, or adopt that branch despite its obsolete handler path?
rationale: The bug is narrow and source-reproducible, but an open PR with closing syntax still points at this issue and is not a safe landing branch, so automation should not create another fix PR until maintainers decide how to dispose of that candidate.

options.title: Close and replace the stale cross-repo candidate
options.body: Close or supersede `https://github.com/BingqingLyu/openclaw/pull/1564`, then queue a fresh narrow fix against `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts`.

options.title: Adopt and rewrite the open candidate
options.body: A maintainer can take over the open cross-repo branch and rewrite it to the current runtime path, but that likely discards most of the submitted diff.

options.title: Wait for the contributor
options.body: Leave the issue blocked on the open cross-repo PR, accepting that the issue remains unfixed while the branch stays conflicting and obsolete.

recommendation.title: Close and replace the stale cross-repo candidate
recommendation.body: Close or supersede `https://github.com/BingqingLyu/openclaw/pull/1564`, then queue a fresh narrow fix against `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts`.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the approval lifecycle refactor that owns the current runtime path and are the best history-backed owner for deciding the branch cleanup route.
